report.releaseDate: 16 Nov 2026 (board-approved 13 Nov 2026; PSE: BLOOM; FY end 31 Dec)
report.currency: PHP (Philippine peso); tables in PHP millions with USD equivalents in parentheses at USD/PHP 63.94
report.verdict: A hold-flattered but genuinely cleaner quarter. Consolidated EBITDA rose 64% YoY to P3.15bn (~$49m) on a 22.9% margin (+770bps), but P350m (~$5.5m) of that is VIP hold running at 3.37% against the 2.85% the company itself calls normal; hold-normalised EBITDA was +32% in Q3 and -5% over nine months, mass-table GGR fell 8%, and visitation dropped 4-9% at both Solaire properties. The P77bn (~$1.21bn) net-debt stack at ~6x annualised EBITDA (our estimate), with the P72bn facility's amortisation tripling from year three, remains the thesis constraint — the shares fell 4.8% to P1.79 on a day the PSEi hit a six-year low.

kpis.label: Net loss (Q3, consolidated)
kpis.delta: vs P1.75bn loss 3Q25; vs P345m loss 2Q26

summary: **Headline: EBITDA +64% YoY to P3.15bn (~$49m), net loss narrowed to P445m (~$7.0m) from P1.75bn.** Net revenue +8.6% to P13.75bn (~$215m), GGR +4.8% to P15.32bn (~$240m), cash opex -1.2% to P10.60bn (~$166m). Sequentially EBITDA fell 8% from 2Q26's P3.43bn (~$54m) and the net loss widened from P345m (~$5.4m). No published sell-side consensus could be verified for a PSE-listed name of this size, so 'beat/miss' is not assessable; versus the prior-year quarter the operating turnaround is unambiguous.

**Hold did the heavy lifting: VIP hold 3.37% vs 2.29% in 3Q25 and the 2.85% 'normal'.** Company-disclosed hold-normalised EBITDA was P2.80bn (~$44m), +31.8% YoY, with reported EBITDA 12.5% above it. On nine months the picture inverts: reported EBITDA +8.1% to P9.55bn (~$149m) but hold-normalised EBITDA -5.4% to P8.53bn (~$133m), margin 21.5% vs 22.6%. The underlying business is not yet growing.

**Volumes were flat, not growing.** Consolidated rolling chip +1.2% to P77.9bn (~$1.22bn), mass drop +1.9% to P15.6bn (~$244m), slot coin-in +0.8% to P121.2bn (~$1.90bn). Visitation fell 4.3% at Solaire Entertainment City (1.13m) and 8.5% at Solaire Quezon City (1.03m); F&B covers fell 5.7% and 12.3% respectively. Revenue per visitor is rising; the funnel is shrinking.

**Mass tables are the weak link: GGR -8.4% to P5.49bn (~$86m) on hold of 35.2% vs 39.1%.** SQC mass GGR fell 19.1% on 3.5% lower drop; SEC mass GGR fell 2.5% despite 6.1% higher drop as hold slid to 41.1% from 44.8% (and from an outlier 55.3% in 2Q26). We estimate mass hold at prior-year levels would have added ~P0.6bn (~$9.6m) of GGR — a partial offset to the VIP hold windfall that the company does not normalise for.

**Promotional intensity cut: contra-revenue -10.1% to P3.05bn (~$48m), 19.9% of GGR vs 23.2% (and 22.8% in 2Q26).** The 17-Q attributes it to lower rebates and promotions to mass patrons. This P343m (~$5.4m) swing is roughly 28% of the YoY EBITDA improvement and is a management choice, not luck — though it coincides with the mass-volume softness above.

**Cost programme is delivering, but is unquantified.** Cash opex fell 1.2% YoY and 0.5% QoQ to P10.60bn (~$166m) — 77.1% of net revenue vs 84.8% — via advertising & promotions, outside services, utilities and cost of sales; 9M cash opex +1.7% to P31.38bn (~$491m). No bad-debt provisions were booked in 3Q26, 2Q26 or 3Q25. Management gives no savings target, amount or end-year; the 'programme' is a run-rate discipline rather than a sized plan.

**Q3 EBITDA bridge (3Q25 → 3Q26): P1,923m + GGR P703m − PFRS15 allocation P72m + lower contra P343m + non-gaming P119m + lower cash opex P133m = P3,149m.** Gaming (net) explains P974m (~$15m) of the P1,226m (~$19m) improvement, of which ~P350m is above-normal VIP hold.

**Below EBITDA: interest expense -5.4% to P1.93bn (~$30m), a P109m (~$1.7m) saving; 9M saving P519m (~$8.1m).** D&A flat at P1.89bn (~$30m); FX gain P217m (~$3.4m) vs P247m. Interest cover (EBITDA/interest) is 1.6x in Q3 and 1.7x over 9M — thin. Management explicitly flagged 'rising benchmark rates' as a risk to future debt-service costs; P68.2bn (~$1.07bn) of the P72bn facility is floating (3M BVAL/BSP TDF + 1.75%), the P40bn facility was converted to fixed.

**9M net loss P915m (~$14.3m) vs net income P160m (~$2.5m), swung by one-offs:** 1Q25 carried a P2.9bn (~$45m) non-cash gain on the P40bn facility modification; 1Q26 carried a P403m (~$6.3m) gain on the Jeju Sun casino-licence sale. Attributable 9M loss P947m (~$14.8m); LPS P0.089 (~$0.0014) vs EPS P0.016.

**Guidance: none, old or new — Bloomberry does not issue numerical guidance.** The Q4 message is qualitative: 'mid-way into the final quarter … focused on driving revenue growth and further optimizing our cost structure' (Razon). Our FY26E EBITDA is ~P12.4-12.5bn (~$195m) with a ~P1.4-1.6bn (~$23m) net loss (estimate, see Forecast).

**Solaire Resort Entertainment City (SEC): EBITDA +60% to P1.98bn (~$31m), margin 22.4% (+730bps).** GGR +3.8% to P10.38bn (~$162m) entirely from VIP hold (3.00% vs 2.25%); rolling chip -5.0%; mass GGR -2.5%; slots +1.0%. Net profit P351m (~$5.5m) vs P411m loss. 9M EBITDA -1.2% to P6.30bn (~$99m).

**Solaire Resort Quezon City (SQC): EBITDA +55% to P1.22bn (~$19m), margin 25.7% (+740bps) — now the higher-margin property.** GGR +7.1% to P4.94bn (~$77m): VIP rolling chip +92% at a 6.08% hold (VIP GGR +315%), slots +12.8%, mass -19.1%. Still a P771m (~$12.1m) net loss after P1.19bn D&A and P800m interest; needs ~P2.0bn quarterly EBITDA to break even at the net line. 9M EBITDA +24.7% to P3.66bn (~$57m).

**Non-gaming +3.6% to P3.46bn (~$54m); occupancy 77.7% SEC / 77.8% SQC.** Hotel & F&B +4.3% to P1.99bn (~$31m), retail & others +0.9% to P1.40bn (~$22m) (SQC retail -18%). Cash share of hotel revenue fell at both properties (SEC 43.1%, SQC 34.2%) — more rooms being comped to support the floor.

**Balance sheet: cash P30.35bn (~$475m), debt P107.4bn (~$1.68bn), net debt P77.1bn (~$1.21bn), down P1.8bn YTD.** Net debt/equity (company definition) 1.71x vs 1.76x at Dec-25 and 1.66x at Sep-25; covenant compliance confirmed. Current portion of long-term debt jumped to P5.52bn (~$86m) from P2.23bn as the P72bn facility enters year-3 amortisation (P6.48bn/yr (~$101m) vs P2.16bn in years 1-2). Our estimate of net debt/annualised EBITDA is ~6.1x.

**Cash flow: 9M operating cash flow +26% to P10.02bn (~$157m); capex -21% to P2.50bn (~$39m); interest paid P4.95bn (~$77m); principal P1.72bn (~$27m); no dividend (P893m (~$14m) paid in 9M25).** Cash rose P3.84bn (~$60m), but P3.0bn of that is net new short-term BDO loans (P8.0bn drawn, P5.0bn repaid). Free cash flow after debt service was ~P0.85bn (~$13m) — essentially break-even.

**Portfolio: Jeju Sun's casino licence has been sold; the Korean unit is now a hotel.** Demerger into Heaven Co. and sale to Blue One completed 4 March 2026 for KRW 10.0bn (KRW 7.0bn received; KRW 3.0bn due by 27 Feb 2027; USD not converted — KRW rate not verified). Jeju Sun Q3 EBITDA P31m (~$0.5m) vs an LBITDA of P15m; GGR nil.

**Online: platform churn, zero disclosure.** MegaFUNalo! (launched June 2025) was shut on 1 May 2026; in-house FUNaloMax soft-launched 6 April and formally launched 3 July 2026; OnlyFun launched October 2026 under the 'Solaire Online' umbrella. No online revenue, GGR, actives or marketing split is disclosed — a gap given the capital and promotional spend going in.

**Land bank: Solaire Properties has bought 223 lots / 2.04m sqm in Paniman, Ternate (Cavite) for a third integrated resort; 'development timeline yet to be finalized'.** Option value, but also a capital-allocation overhang at ~6x leverage. Bloomberry is a subsidiary of Prime Strategic Holdings (Razon); 11.53bn shares outstanding.

**Share price: -4.8% to P1.79 on 16 Nov vs PSEi -2.0% to 5,481.88 (lowest close in 6+ years, 'stagflation fears').** Market cap ~P20.6bn (~$323m); EV ~P97.7bn (~$1.53bn), ~7.7x annualised 9M EBITDA (our estimate). The equity is a thin sliver on a large debt stack — hold volatility and rates dominate the stock.

**Thesis read-through: operating leverage is real (every P1 of net revenue growth dropped through at >100% this quarter), but the base is volume-flat and hold-dependent.** De-leveraging requires EBITDA above ~P14bn/yr (~$219m) to cover ~P7.7bn interest, ~P5.6-6.5bn amortisation and ~P3.3bn capex; FY26E lands ~P12.5bn. The P30bn cash cushion buys 2-3 years, but the path to equity value runs through mass-volume recovery at both properties, not through hold.

**Data gaps flagged:** no market-share data (PAGCOR industry GGR not retrievable this session), no consensus, no online KPIs, no FY25 EBITDA for an LTM multiple; the 17-Q narrative cites a 3Q25 LPS of P0.134 against P0.165 in its own tables and the press release (we use P0.165); the 17-Q repeats SEC's 9M F&B covers (1,669,859) under SQC — treated as a typo.

segments.name: Solaire Resort Entertainment City (SEC) — Parañaque, Entertainment City
segments.headline: EBITDA +60% to P1.98bn (~$31m) on a 22.4% margin, but GGR growth of 3.8% came entirely from a 3.00% VIP hold; rolling chip -5%, mass GGR -2.5%, visitation -4.3%.
narrative: Solaire Resort Entertainment City delivered GGR of P10.38bn (~$162m), up 3.8% YoY but down 9.7% on the quarter, and the composition matters more than the headline. VIP rolling-chip volume fell 5.0% YoY to P68.5bn (~$1.07bn) and 4% QoQ, yet VIP GGR rose 26.3% to P2.05bn (~$32m) because hold came in at 3.00% against 2.25% a year ago and the 2.85% the company treats as normal; management concedes in the 17-Q that on a hold-normalised basis VIP revenue would have grown just 6.1%. VIP therefore added P427m (~$6.7m) against a total GGR increase of only P378m (~$5.9m) — the rest of the floor shrank. VIP is now 20% of SEC GGR versus 16% a year ago.

Mass tables were the soft spot. Drop rose 6.1% YoY to P9.18bn (~$144m) and 21% QoQ, but hold slipped to 41.1% from 44.8% (and from an unusually high 55.3% in 2Q26), so mass GGR fell 2.5% to P3.78bn (~$59m) and 10% sequentially. A 14-point sequential swing in mass hold on a 21% jump in drop is not explained anywhere in the filings; the pattern is consistent with a mix shift toward premium-mass direct play (higher drop, lower hold) rather than pure luck, and we would want management to clarify before treating the drop growth as a demand signal. Slots were steady: coin-in +0.6% to P78.1bn (~$1.22bn), hold flat at 5.8%, GGR +1.0% to P4.55bn (~$71m). Slots are now 44% of SEC GGR, mass 36% and VIP 20%.

Below GGR the quarter was helped by a lighter promotional load. Contra-revenue accounts (rebates, commissions and promotional allowances) fell 9.7% YoY to P2.39bn (~$37m), or 23.0% of GGR versus 26.4% in 3Q25 and 26.6% in 2Q26, which the 17-Q attributes to lower rebates and promotions to mass patrons. After PFRS 15 allocations of P1.34bn (~$21m), net gaming revenue rose 8.5% to P6.65bn (~$104m) and net revenue 7.5% to P8.83bn (~$138m), 75% of it gaming. Cash operating expenses were cut 1.8% YoY to P6.85bn (~$107m) — 77.6% of net revenue against 84.9% — and were flat QoQ, producing EBITDA of P1.98bn (~$31m), +60.2% YoY but -17.4% QoQ, at a 22.4% margin (+730bps YoY, -360bps QoQ). After D&A of P669m (~$10m), interest of P1.13bn (~$18m) and a P169m (~$2.6m) FX gain, SEC posted a net profit of P351m (~$5.5m) against a P411m loss a year ago and P667m in 2Q26.

Non-gaming revenue grew 4.7% to P2.17bn (~$34m) and 10.8% QoQ: hotel and F&B +0.7% to P1.11bn (~$17m), retail and others +8.2% to P1.01bn (~$16m), interest income P50m. Occupancy was 77.7% (74.3% in 3Q25; 78.4% in 2Q26), while the cash share of hotel revenue slipped to 43.1% from 45.1% — more rooms are being comped to gaming patrons — and the cash share of F&B rose to 59.9% from 56.9%. Covers fell 5.7% to 515,728 but the average check rose 6.7% to P1,268 (~$19.8). Visitation fell 4.3% to 1.13m for the quarter, which for a property that is 80% mass and slots is the number to watch.

On a nine-month view SEC is flat. GGR was P31.85bn (~$498m, -0.2%): VIP GGR +13% to P6.61bn (~$103m) on a 3.43% hold (+81bps) masking a 14% fall in rolling chip to P193.0bn (~$3.02bn); mass GGR -6% to P11.86bn (~$185m) on 2% lower drop and 2.3pts lower hold; slots flat at P13.38bn (~$209m) on 11% lower coin-in offset by 0.7pts higher hold. Contra was 24.5% of GGR (24.8%). Net revenue was P26.49bn (~$414m, +0.2%), cash opex +0.6% to P20.18bn (~$316m), EBITDA P6.30bn (~$99m, -1.2%) at a 23.8% margin (24.1%), and net profit P1.49bn (~$23m, +59%) on P313m lower interest. Occupancy was 76.7% (72.6%). Our read: the cost base is being held and promotional discipline is real, but the top line is volume-flat and hold-dependent, and SEC has yet to show it can grow visitation against cannibalisation from Quezon City and a softer Manila consumer. Market share: not disclosed and PAGCOR industry GGR was not retrievable this session (n/a).

segments.name: Solaire Resort Quezon City (SQC, formerly Solaire Resort North) — opened 25 May 2024
segments.headline: EBITDA +55% to P1.22bn (~$19m) at a group-best 25.7% margin, driven by a 6.08% VIP hold on 92% higher rolling chip and slots +13%; mass GGR -19% and visitation -8.5%; still a P771m (~$12m) net loss after D&A and interest.
narrative: Solaire Resort Quezon City produced GGR of P4.94bn (~$77m), +7.1% YoY and +0.7% QoQ, but the growth came almost entirely from the VIP line. Rolling chip nearly doubled to P9.40bn (~$147m) (+91.5% YoY, +10% QoQ) and hold was an outsized 6.08% against 2.80% a year ago and the 2.85% norm, so VIP GGR rose 315% to P571m (~$8.9m). Normalised for hold, management says VIP revenue would have grown 91.5% — i.e. in line with volume — which does argue that SQC is building a genuine premium-direct book, albeit from a small base (VIP is 11% of SQC GGR, up from 3%). On nine months VIP hold is 4.82%, so the property has been running well above normal all year; the P1.11bn (~$17m) 9M VIP GGR would be roughly P0.66bn at 2.85%.

The mass floor went the other way. Mass drop fell 3.5% YoY to P6.44bn (~$101m) (+19% QoQ) and hold dropped to 26.6% from 31.8%, so mass GGR fell 19.1% to P1.71bn (~$27m) (-4% QoQ) — the weakest line in the group. Slots, 54% of SQC GGR, were the offset: coin-in +1.2% to P43.1bn (~$674m), hold up 0.7pts to 6.2%, GGR +12.8% to P2.65bn (~$41m) (flat QoQ). Visitation fell 8.5% to 1.03m and F&B covers 12.3% to 546,567, so the property is doing more revenue per visitor rather than drawing more people — a pattern that fits a maturing ramp rather than an expanding catchment, and one that sits awkwardly with the 'continued ramp-up' language in the 17-Q.

Contra-revenue was P665m (~$10m), 13.5% of GGR (16.3% in 3Q25, 14.2% in 2Q26) — structurally far lighter than SEC's 23% given the mass/slot mix — and PFRS 15 allocations were P636m (~$10m); net gaming revenue grew 14.4% to P3.64bn (~$57m). Non-gaming slipped 1.4% to P1.11bn (~$17m): hotel and F&B +9.1% to P744m (~$12m) on higher REVPAR and 77.8% occupancy (68.4% a year ago, but down from 85.6% in 2Q26), while retail and others fell 18.0% to P352m (~$5.5m). Cash revenue shares were lower — 34.2% of hotel (39.8%) and 67.8% of F&B (71.5%) — pointing to heavier comping to support the gaming floor. Net revenue rose 10.2% to P4.75bn (~$74m).

Cash opex was held flat YoY at P3.53bn (~$55m) (+2.8% QoQ), 74.3% of net revenue versus 81.7%, taking EBITDA up 55.0% to P1.22bn (~$19m) at a 25.7% margin (+740bps YoY; 27.0% in 2Q26) — SQC is now the higher-margin property. But the capital structure beneath it remains heavy: D&A of P1.19bn (~$19m) consumes essentially all of the EBITDA and interest of P800m (~$12.5m) pushes the property to a net loss of P771m (~$12.1m), compared with P1.23bn a year ago and P738m in 2Q26. SQC needs roughly P2.0bn (~$31m) of quarterly EBITDA to break even at the net line, versus P1.22bn today. On nine months its net loss is P2.35bn (~$37m) versus P228m, though the 2025 figure was flattered by the P2.9bn (~$45m) non-cash gain on the P40bn facility modification booked at this entity.

Nine-month SQC GGR rose 5.7% to P14.54bn (~$227m): VIP GGR +36% on 27% higher rolling chip (P23.0bn, ~$360m), mass GGR -8% to P5.49bn (~$86m) on 13% lower drop despite 1.8pts better hold, slots +14% to P7.94bn (~$124m) on 9% higher coin-in. Contra was 13.7% of GGR (15.9%). Net revenue +8.5% to P13.98bn (~$219m), cash opex +3.7% to P10.32bn (~$161m), EBITDA +24.7% to P3.66bn (~$57m) at 26.2% (22.8%); occupancy 80.5% (62.6%). The property is earning its EBITDA ramp through slots, premium play and cost control, but the 19% decline in mass GGR and the 8.5% fall in visitors are the numbers that need to reverse before it contributes to group net income. Market share within Metro Manila: n/a (not disclosed).

F&B covers fell 12.3% to 546,567; the property is doing more revenue per visitor rather than drawing more people.
Pattern fits a maturing ramp rather than an expanding catchment and sits awkwardly with the 'continued ramp-up' language in the 17-Q.

blocks.heading: Contra and non-gaming
blocks.takeaway: Contra-revenue was a light 13.5% of GGR at P665m (~$10m), while non-gaming slipped 1.4% to P1.11bn (~$17m) with heavier comping.
points: Contra 13.5% of GGR versus 16.3% in 3Q25 and 14.2% in 2Q26, structurally far lighter than SEC's 23% given the mass/slot mix.
PFRS 15 allocations P636m (~$10m); net gaming revenue +14.4% to P3.64bn (~$57m).
Hotel and F&B +9.1% to P744m (~$12m) on higher REVPAR and 77.8% occupancy (68.4% a year ago; 85.6% in 2Q26); retail and others -18.0% to P352m (~$5.5m).
Cash share of hotel 34.2% (39.8%) and F&B 67.8% (71.5%), pointing to heavier comping to support the gaming floor.
Net revenue rose 10.2% to P4.75bn (~$74m).

blocks.heading: EBITDA and net loss
blocks.takeaway: EBITDA rose 55.0% to P1.22bn (~$19m) at a group-best 25.7% margin, but D&A and interest leave a P771m (~$12.1m) net loss.
points: Cash opex flat YoY at P3.53bn (~$55m) (+2.8% QoQ), 74.3% of net revenue versus 81.7%.
Margin +740bps YoY; 27.0% in 2Q26; SQC is now the higher-margin property.
D&A of P1.19bn (~$19m) consumes essentially all EBITDA; interest P800m (~$12.5m); net loss compares with P1.23bn a year ago and P738m in 2Q26.
SQC needs roughly P2.0bn (~$31m) of quarterly EBITDA to break even at the net line, versus P1.22bn today.
Nine-month net loss P2.35bn (~$37m) versus P228m, though 2025 was flattered by a P2.9bn (~$45m) non-cash gain on the P40bn facility modification.

blocks.heading: Nine-month view
blocks.takeaway: Nine-month GGR rose 5.7% to P14.54bn (~$227m) and EBITDA 24.7% to P3.66bn (~$57m) at 26.2%, but mass and visitation declines must reverse.
points: VIP GGR +36% on 27% higher rolling chip (P23.0bn, ~$360m); mass GGR -8% to P5.49bn (~$86m) on 13% lower drop despite 1.8pts better hold.
Slots +14% to P7.94bn (~$124m) on 9% higher coin-in; contra 13.7% of GGR (15.9%).
Net revenue +8.5% to P13.98bn (~$219m); cash opex +3.7% to P10.32bn (~$161m); margin 26.2% (22.8%); occupancy 80.5% (62.6%).
EBITDA ramp is earned through slots, premium play and cost control, but the 19% mass GGR decline and 8.5% visitor fall must reverse before SQC contributes to group net income.
Market share within Metro Manila: n/a (not disclosed).

segments.name: Jeju Sun (Korea), Online platforms & Corporate / non-operating subsidiaries
segments.headline: Jeju Sun is now a casino-free hotel (EBITDA P31m vs LBITDA P15m) after the KRW 10bn licence sale; corporate LBITDA P83m; online (FUNaloMax, OnlyFun) is being rebuilt in-house with zero KPI disclosure; Paniman land bank at 2.04m sqm.
narrative: Jeju Sun is now a hotel, not a casino. Golden & Luxury (96.2% held via Solaire Korea) spun its casino into Heaven Co. Ltd. and sold it to Blue One Ltd.; the demerger completed on 4 March 2026 with KRW 7.0bn of the KRW 10.0bn price received and KRW 3.0bn due by 27 February 2027 (USD equivalents not converted — KRW rate not verified this session). Heaven continues to operate the casino on the Jeju property under a lease until it finds a new site. The group booked a P404m (~$6.3m) gain in 1Q26 on the sale (in 'Others'), which flatters 9M net income. Q3 GGR was nil (P3.8m in 3Q25); hotel and F&B revenue rose 10.5% to P126m (~$2.0m) and retail/others to P37m (~$0.6m), giving net revenue of P163m (~$2.5m), +15.9%. With cash opex down 15% to P132m (~$2.1m), EBITDA was P31m (~$0.5m) against an LBITDA of P15m, and the unit posted a P7m (~$0.1m) net profit versus a P36m loss. Nine-month EBITDA is break-even (vs an LBITDA of P116m), and the P334m (~$5.2m) 9M net profit is almost entirely the licence gain. The exit removes a chronic loss-maker; what remains is a 202-room hotel with limited strategic relevance and residual Korean land (Muui/Silmi islands) whose conversion is still pending.

Corporate and non-operating subsidiaries (Solaire Properties, Solaire Resort Corp, Bloomberry Cruise Terminals, Solaire Korea, Muui) absorbed P97m (~$1.5m) of cash opex in the quarter (+10% YoY) for an LBITDA of P83m (~$1.3m), broadly flat on P86m; a P47m (~$0.7m) FX gain narrowed the net loss to P33m (~$0.5m) from P74m. Nine-month corporate LBITDA widened 14% to P415m (~$6.5m) on P431m (~$6.7m) of opex (+17%). The main item here is land: Solaire Properties has now acquired 223 lots totalling 2,036,665 sqm in Paniman, Ternate, Cavite (the 2022 headline agreement covered 2.80m sqm at an average P2,700/sqm (~$42)), for an integrated resort with casino, hotel, golf and mixed-use whose 'development timeline is yet to be finalized'. That is an option on a third property, but also a capital-allocation overhang for a group already at ~6x net debt/EBITDA (our estimate) with no dividend paid this year. The Solaire Cruise Center and Yacht Harbor (BCTI) remains a designated Tourism Enterprise Zone with no disclosed spend.

The online pivot is real but unquantified. MegaFUNalo!, the broad-mass digital platform launched on 8 June 2025 on a third-party stack, was shut on 1 May 2026 and replaced by the in-house FUNaloMax (soft launch 6 April, official launch 3 July 2026); OnlyFun followed in October 2026, all under a 'portfolio of online gaming entertainment platforms led by the Solaire Online brand'. No revenue, GGR, actives, ARPU or marketing split is disclosed for online — it sits inside SEC/SQC gaming revenue under the same PAGCOR licence — so we cannot assess the return on the platform rebuild, or whether the P343m (~$5.4m) YoY reduction in contra-revenue reflects promotional spend being redirected to digital. Given continuing legislative scrutiny of online gambling in the Philippines (status not re-verified for this note), the absence of online KPIs is a disclosure gap investors should press on. Regulatory framing is otherwise unchanged: both Philippine properties operate under BRHI's PAGCOR licence, which runs with PAGCOR's franchise to 11 July 2033; licence fees are paid on GGR in lieu of taxes plus a 2% remittance to the cultural foundation and a 5% fee on F&B/retail/hotel non-gaming revenue.

highlights.text: **Cost discipline is holding against inflation:** cash opex -1.2% YoY and -0.5% QoQ to P10.60bn (~$166m), 77.1% of net revenue vs 84.8%; 9M +1.7%. SEC opex -1.8%, SQC flat. No bad-debt provisions for three consecutive quarters; allowances cover 86% of >90-day receivables.

**Promotional intensity down 330bps:** contra-revenue 19.9% of GGR (23.2% in 3Q25, 22.8% in 2Q26), worth P343m (~$5.4m) of the YoY EBITDA uplift; SEC 23.0% (26.4%), SQC 13.5% (16.3%). A management lever, not luck — but it coincides with softer mass volumes.

**SQC margin ramp is real:** EBITDA +55% to P1.22bn (~$19m) at 25.7% (+740bps), with slots GGR +12.8% on 1.2% higher coin-in and a 6.2% hold; 9M EBITDA +24.7% at 26.2%. Rolling chip +92% shows a premium-direct book forming.
**Interest burden falling:** Q3 interest expense -5.4% to P1.93bn (~$30m), P109m (~$1.7m) saved; 9M P519m (~$8.1m) saved; interest paid -13.5% to P4.95bn (~$77m). P40bn facility now fixed-rate.

**Cash generation improved:** 9M operating cash flow +26% to P10.02bn (~$157m) on higher EBITDA and lower working capital; capex -21% to P2.50bn (~$39m); cash up P3.84bn (~$60m) to P30.35bn (~$475m); net debt down P1.8bn YTD to P77.1bn (~$1.21bn).
**Non-gaming steady at SEC:** revenue +4.7% to P2.17bn (~$34m), occupancy 77.7% (+340bps), retail +8.2%, average check +6.7% to P1,268 (~$19.8); group hotel & F&B +4.3%.
**Jeju Sun de-risked:** casino licence sold (KRW 10bn), P404m (~$6.3m) gain booked, unit now EBITDA-positive (P31m vs LBITDA P15m) with 9M LBITDA of P116m eliminated.

lowlights.text: **Hold-flattered:** VIP hold 3.37% vs 2.85% normal added ~P350m (~$5.5m) to EBITDA; hold-normalised EBITDA +32% YoY in Q3 but -5.4% over 9M (P8.53bn, ~$133m) with margin down 110bps to 21.5%. SQC's 6.08% quarterly / 4.82% 9M VIP hold will not persist. Every 50bps of VIP hold ≈ P390m (~$6.1m) of quarterly GGR.

**Mass tables shrinking:** group mass GGR -8.4% to P5.49bn (~$86m), 9M -6.9%; SQC mass GGR -19.1% on 3.5% lower drop; SEC mass hold swung 55.3% → 41.1% QoQ on +21% drop with no explanation — possible premium-mass mix shift or reclassification that management should clarify.

**Visitation falling at both properties:** SEC -4.3% to 1.13m, SQC -8.5% to 1.03m; covers -5.7% / -12.3%; 9M SQC visitors -3.2%. Rising spend per head is masking a narrowing funnel in a weak consumer backdrop (PSEi at a six-year low on stagflation concerns).

**Leverage and amortisation step-up:** net debt P77.1bn (~$1.21bn), ~6.1x annualised EBITDA (est.), interest cover 1.6x; current portion of LTD up to P5.52bn (~$86m) from P2.23bn as the P72bn facility's year-3 amortisation triples to P6.48bn/yr (~$101m). P68.2bn (~$1.07bn) floating at BVAL/TDF + 1.75%; management flagged rising benchmark rates.

**SQC still loss-making below EBITDA:** net loss P771m (~$12.1m) in Q3 (P738m in 2Q26) and P2.35bn (~$37m) over 9M; D&A of P1.19bn/qtr plus P800m interest require ~P2.0bn quarterly EBITDA to break even vs P1.22bn delivered.

**Retail & others weak:** SQC -18.0% to P352m (~$5.5m), 9M -15.5%; group 9M retail & others -6.3% to P3.86bn (~$60m). Cash share of hotel revenue falling at both properties (SEC 43.1%, SQC 34.2%) as more rooms are comped.

**Disclosure thin for the risks being taken:** no numerical guidance, no cost-programme sizing, no online KPIs despite a platform rebuild (FUNaloMax, OnlyFun), no market-share data; 17-Q narrative misstates 3Q25 LPS (P0.134 vs P0.165 in tables) and duplicates SEC covers under SQC. No dividend paid in 9M26 vs P893m (~$14m) in 9M25.

forecast.intro: There is no guidance to bridge: Bloomberry has never issued numerical guidance and did not start this quarter. The only forward statements are qualitative — Chairman/CEO Enrique Razon Jr. says the group is 'mid-way into the final quarter … focused on driving revenue growth and further optimizing our cost structure', and flags that 'rising benchmark rates' could lift future debt-service costs. In lieu of a guidance bridge, the bridge below reconciles the YoY change in Q3 EBITDA (P1,923m → P3,149m, ~$30m → ~$49m): gaming contributed P974m (~$15m) net (GGR +P703m, PFRS 15 allocation −P72m, lower contra +P343m), of which ~P350m is above-normal VIP hold; non-gaming added P119m (~$1.9m) and cash-opex savings P133m (~$2.1m). The division that drove the quarter was SEC (EBITDA +P744m, ~$11.6m) on VIP hold and lower promos; SQC added P434m (~$6.8m) on VIP hold, slots and flat costs; Jeju and corporate were immaterial (+P49m combined).

forecast.view: **Q4 2026E (our estimate):** we assume VIP rolling chip of ~P78bn (~$1.22bn) at a normalised 2.85% hold → VIP GGR ~P2.2bn (~$34m), mass GGR ~P5.7bn (~$89m) as hold recovers toward ~37% on seasonally firmer December drop, and slots ~P7.4bn (~$116m) → GGR ~P15.3bn (~$239m), flat YoY and QoQ. With contra at ~21% of GGR and PFRS 15 at ~13%, net gaming is ~P10.1bn and net revenue ~P13.6bn (~$213m). Cash opex of ~P10.7bn (~$167m) yields **EBITDA of ~P2.9bn (~$45m), range P2.7-3.2bn depending on hold, i.e. 21% margin**, and a net loss of ~P0.5-0.7bn (~$8-11m) after ~P1.9bn D&A and ~P1.9bn interest. **FY2026E: net revenue ~P54.5bn (~$852m), EBITDA ~P12.4-12.5bn (~$195m), net loss ~P1.4-1.6bn (~$23m).** Margin direction: flat-to-down sequentially as hold normalises; up ~100bps YoY for the full year on the cost base. **Leverage direction: flat.** On our numbers annual cash needs are ~P7.0-7.7bn interest, ~P5.6-6.5bn scheduled amortisation and ~P3.3bn capex (~P16-17bn, ~$255m) against ~P13bn (~$203m) of operating cash flow, so free cash flow after debt service is roughly −P2-3bn/yr (~$31-47m) and net debt drifts up unless EBITDA grows — net debt/FY26E EBITDA ~6.2x (estimate). The P30.35bn (~$475m) cash pile funds the gap comfortably for 2-3 years, and covenant DSCR is cash-inclusive, so this is a de-leveraging stall rather than a liquidity event. **Swing factors:** (1) VIP hold — ±50bps ≈ ±P390m (~$6.1m) quarterly GGR; (2) mass drop/hold mix at SEC; (3) BSP policy rate on P68bn floating debt — ±100bps ≈ ±P0.7bn (~$11m) annual interest; (4) a decision to exercise the one-time fixed-rate conversion on the P72bn facility; (5) Paniman capex timing; (6) any online regulatory change.
watch: VIP hold reversion from 3.37% (6.08% at SQC) toward 2.85%, and whether the P9.4bn SQC rolling-chip book is sticky.
SEC mass hold/drop mix: the 55.3% → 41.1% QoQ swing on +21% drop needs a premium-mass vs grind-mass explanation.
Visitation (SEC -4.3%, SQC -8.5%) and F&B covers through the December peak; PSEi/consumer backdrop.
P72bn facility year-3 amortisation (P6.48bn/yr from ~Q4 2026) and current LTD of P5.52bn; use of the one-time fixed-rate conversion option; BSP rate path.
Online KPIs for FUNaloMax/OnlyFun and any Philippine legislative action on online gambling or payment rails.
Paniman (2.04m sqm) development decision and funding; dividend policy (none paid in 9M26).
Receivables (+P363m YTD to P1.64bn, ~$26m) and collection of the KRW 3.0bn Jeju balance due Feb 2027.
